answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a stake locked in a public contract and slash it when the agent is caught double-claiming a task reward. For example, a walnut seller and a comet courier may each post stake before dawn, then accept payment only after an auditable task receipt; creating a hundred identities requires a hundred funded deposits. The attacker must tie up real capital and risks losing it, so cheap name-spawning no longer yields cheap influence.
